meta.title: Synthetic US conventional purchase mortgage: borrower-agent compute scenarios
meta.status: SYNTHETIC WORKED EXAMPLE. Every count, token size, cache fraction, latency, retry rate, human-time and calendar value in this file is an ASSUMPTION chosen for illustration. None is measured from a real mortgage, sampled from users, or calibrated to any benchmark or public trace.
meta.price_basis: Provider Standard API list prices recorded in COMPUTE-PRICE-NOTES.md (checked 2026-10-17). Outputs are illustrative per-token bills, not subscription charges, not measured compute and not energy.
meta.legal_basis: Waiting periods follow MORTGAGE-AND-FAILURE-EVIDENCE.md (CFPB, 12 CFR 1026.19, IRS IVES). The fifteen fresh human checkpoints are a conservative study choice held fixed across architectures, not a list of statutory requirements. Durations not stated in the ledger are labelled assumptions.
meta.retry_semantics: Each failed action gets exactly one additional repair attempt (expected value rate x actions), and the repair is assumed to succeed. This is not geometric retry-until-success; abandoned or failed tasks are not costed.
meta.schedule_semantics: parallel_critical_path_s is a conditional scheduling estimate, not an optimal DAG critical path: stages run in order, a mixed B stage runs its connector group and then its browser group, and units within a group run up to parallel_width at a time. Background monitoring is excluded.
meta.external_request_semantics: N_external_service_requests counts application-level requests to or from other parties, including incoming event deliveries handled by C; subresource fetches are excluded.

scope.loan: conventional purchase, first lien, one property
scope.employment: both salaried, one employer each (W-2 income only)
scope.document_breakdown: 4 bank statements (2 institutions x 2 months), 2 recent pay stubs, 4 W-2s (2 borrowers x 2 years), 2 photo IDs
scope.service_session_breakdown: 2 deposit institutions, 2 employer/payroll portals, 3 lender portals (the chosen lender's session is reused)
human_only_acts_not_performed_by_agent: closing signature on note and mortgage/deed of trust
property access for the physical appraisal
excluded_from_agent_processing: Loan Estimate delivery wait (lender generally must deliver within 3 business days of application)
Closing Disclosure waiting period (at least 3 business days before consummation; certain changes restart it)
physical appraisal, title and insurance work
lender-side verification vendors (asset, income, employment, IRS IVES) operated under the lender's contracts
human signature, payment and funds transfer
time humans spend waiting between checkpoints

gpt_6_astra_standard.label: GPT-6 Astra, Standard
gpt_6_astra_standard.note: Requests above 272K input are priced higher; the calculator fails a check if any assumed request reaches that size.

claude_opus_5_5_standard.label: Claude Opus 5.5, Standard global, 5-minute cache write
claude_opus_5_5_standard.note: 1-hour cache write is 8 USD/M and is not used here. Output includes billable thinking.

architectures.A_step: Screen-driven agent, one UI action per model response, screenshot observation after each action. Shown as a lower bound on engineering effort, not the fair comparator.
architectures.A_batch: Screen-driven agent that emits a batch of up to b UI actions per response (direct URL navigation, keyboard entry, multi-field fill) and observes once per batch. The fair screen-driven comparator.
architectures.B: Existing direct APIs/connectors (financial-data aggregator, email, calendar, search/fetch, local PDF fill, product-native approval UI) orchestrated by the model; stages without a connector fall back to the A_batch browser path. Routine connector polling may run without the model.
architectures.C: Interoperable domain operations with explicit, machine-checked permission objects executed by ordinary software. The LLM is called only for natural-language goals, comparison narrative, supplier discovery judgement, exception handling, borrower questions and (if disclosures are not machine-readable) document reading.

c_residual_counting_rules.goal_clarification: counted: LLM requests in every architecture
c_residual_counting_rules.supplier_discovery: counted: 1 LLM request per lender to judge entity role and ambiguous registry results
c_residual_counting_rules.ocr_or_document_reading: counted only when c_structured_disclosures is false (Loan Estimate and Closing Disclosure read by the model)
c_residual_counting_rules.exception_handling: counted: 2 LLM requests per exception; exceptions occur at the same rate in every architecture
c_residual_counting_rules.model_based_monitors: not used in C; status changes arrive as events. Each assumed status update costs one external delivery and one deterministic handling operation (0 LLM). Any model reviewer is counted under reviewer_mode for all architectures alike
c_residual_counting_rules.human_clarification: counted as human minutes and as borrower-question model requests in every architecture
c_residual_counting_rules.permission_checks: counted as tool invocations (deterministic), not model requests

stages.label: Goal clarification with both borrowers
stages.note: Four conversational turns in every architecture; C stores the resulting goal/mandate draft deterministically.

stages.label: Authentication / mandate establishment per service session
stages.note: Cold: secure sign-in hand-off/MFA (A), OAuth grant (B), endpoint discovery + credential verification + mandate grant (C); each needs one human intervention. Warm: session or mandate validity check only.

stages.label: Authorised retrieval: two months of statements per deposit institution
stages.note: C: permission check, two record retrievals, local receipt/hash. Connector coverage for B is a scenario parameter; no claim that all banks offer structured access.

stages.label: Authorised retrieval: pay stub and W-2s per employer/payroll portal
stages.note: Consumer-side payroll connector availability is uncertain; central B uses the browser fallback.

stages.label: Supplier discovery and lender entity/role verification
stages.note: Distinguish lender, broker, comparison tool and lead generator before any data is sent. A reads pages via screenshots counted inside per-request input; B reads fetched page text as document tokens.

stages.label: Data preparation and entry of the six application items, per lender
stages.note: No consumer application API is assumed in B (browser fallback); the B api spec is used only in the hypothetical all-API sensitivity. Submission is a consequential write after the lender-specific checkpoint.

stages.label: Official offer gathering: obtain and extract each Loan Estimate
stages.note: Three-page Loan Estimate assumed at 1,500 tokens per page when read by a model. C assumes a machine-readable estimate unless c_structured_disclosures is false.

stages.label: Offer comparison and explanation to borrowers
stages.note: C computes the normalised comparison deterministically and uses the LLM for the narrative and follow-up.

stages.label: Named consent checkpoints: present and record each decision
stages.note: C renders a templated permission object (verb, object, purpose, duration, recipient) and records the decision. Borrower questions at checkpoints are counted in the questions stage.

stages.label: Send intent to proceed to the chosen lender
stages.note: Bound to one lender and one Loan Estimate version; B sends by email where the lender accepts it.

stages.label: Prepare verification consents (2 asset-portal links, 2 IRS 4506-C, 2 employment/income)
stages.note: Agent prepares and transmits; humans select accounts in the vendor portal and sign. B: local PDF fill for 4506-C where available, browser otherwise.

stages.label: Document transfer to the chosen lender, per document
stages.note: Upload, document-type selection, confirm, verify. C: permission check, transfer, receipt verification.

stages.label: Appointment coordination (appraisal access, closing)
stages.note: Counterparts may reply in natural language, so C keeps one LLM request per appointment.

stages.label: Status monitoring during processing (per check)
stages.note: Spread over the processing weeks, so excluded from the schedule estimate. B polls a connector deterministically and wakes the model only for new messages (already counted elsewhere). C receives events: ASSUMPTION that the number of status updates delivered equals monitoring_polls (10/20/40); each is one external delivery plus deterministic handling, 0 LLM. Real update frequencies may differ.

stages.label: Underwriting clarification round (two conditions)
stages.note: Interpret notice, locate sourced records, draft explanation for borrower attestation, submit two responses. Residual LLM work remains in C.

stages.label: Final review: Closing Disclosure against chosen Loan Estimate
stages.note: Five-page disclosure at 1,500 tokens per page when model-read. C diffs structured fields and explains differences.

stages.label: Exceptions (portal error, nonstandard form, ambiguous request), per exception
stages.note: Exceptions are a property of the world, so the same count applies to every architecture.

energy.status: Coefficient sensitivity only. Units are thousands of prefill-token equivalents (kPTE): 1 kPTE = energy to prefill 1,000 uncached input tokens on whatever deployment the reader specifies. Not a measured footprint for any provider or model.

absolute_conversion.note: Enable only with deployment-specific values. Training energy is excluded and must not be added per call.

unconverted_drivers: server-side record generation and permission services

hand_checks.note: Values computed by hand from the inventory before the script was run. A mismatch is a discrepancy to investigate, not a tolerance to widen.
